source.title: TWO-WHEELER-ENG-001: co-design bicycle, e-bike, motorcycle and microfactory benchmarks
source.body:
## Mission

Create an evidence-bounded, two-wheeler engineering benchmark that jointly evaluates bicycle/e-bike/motorcycle design and the production/service systems that make those vehicles affordable and maintainable.

This is a specialization of existing owners, not a competing vehicle solver or factory scheduler.

## Paradigm shift

Optimize for **verified mobility delivered over the vehicle's service life**, not one headline specification such as mass, top speed, range or initial price. Co-design the product, production cell, service tasks, parts network and end-of-life path. Preserve a Pareto frontier rather than hiding incompatible goals in one weighted score.

## Reuse existing owners

- Transport architecture: #6244
- Road/off-road tire/contact, braking, handling and qualification semantics: #6247
- Vehicle/logistics hardware manufacturing qualification: #5985
- Low-consequence physical qualification ladder: #6254
- Factory scheduler and manufacturing-value work: #7677 / PR #7678; #7608
- Repairability-first personal/family transport research: PR #7751
- Symtropy mobility simulation/whole-life optimization: PR #1762 and issues #1601, #1773, #1780
- Mycelix vehicle dossier and maintenance-event evidence: PR #5131 / issue #5132

Do not duplicate road dynamics, physics, battery/electric-machine models, material science, scheduling, lifecycle optimization, service history or authority semantics. Add two-wheeler-specific profiles only where existing contracts demonstrably lack them.

## Work packages

1. **Start with a conventional utility/commuter bicycle** as the low-energy anchor; define the user/duty-cycle envelope, freeze comparable baselines and document exclusions. A cargo-bike profile must not silently inherit a general bicycle standard's applicability.
2. Add a cargo/utility bicycle profile, then an electrically assisted bicycle profile with its electrical safety and jurisdiction-specific classification kept separate from mechanical qualification.
3. Only after the contract is stable, add a bounded commuter/utility motorcycle profile with motorcycle-specific braking, vehicle dynamics, E/E functional-safety, type-approval and physical test gates.
4. Co-design product and manufacturing cell: fabrication route, fixture access, tolerances, inspection, assembly, first-pass yield, material utilization, worker/tool capability, serviceability and parts resilience.
5. Compare volumes of 1, 10, 25, 100 and 1,000 units; keep quoted prices, catalog prices, modeled costs and observed production costs distinct.
6. Emit reproducible, digest-bound scenarios and adversarial controls that make missing evidence, changed configuration, incompatible units, invalid model scope, unavailable tools/parts and safety-gate regressions fail closed.

## Proposed scorecard (research targets, not achieved results or standards)

- **Evidence integrity:** zero false accepts across the frozen negative-control suite; all output claims identify configuration, model revision, input digest, evidence class, uncertainty and applicability.
- **Product trade space:** report a Pareto frontier for mass, durability, useful payload, energy/fuel, comfort/fit, repair time, downtime, lifecycle cost and environmental burden. Safety/legal constraints are hard gates.
- **Model validation:** report errors by observable and operating envelope against held-out physical data; target <=10% error only for specifically defined observables after adequate independent data exist. No aggregate accuracy claim.
- **Repairability:** freeze at least 10 common tasks; measure diagnosis, hands-on work, verification, rework, tools, parts lead time and vehicle downtime separately; target >=25% reduction in median and P90 task time against a matched baseline, subject to safety-equivalent procedures.
- **Microfactory economics:** report yield-adjusted cost per conforming unit and sensitivity to labor, scrap, rework, supplier delay, equipment amortization and volume. A candidate target is >=30% lower assembly touch labor at 25+ units with no reduction in acceptance quality; validate with observed runs before claiming savings.
- **Lifecycle and locality:** compare whole-life cost per 1,000 completed km and service continuity under parts/fuel/electricity/cash-flow shocks. Keep local sourcing percentage separate from actual renewable productive closure.
- **Robustness:** test wet/low-friction surface, payload and CG shifts, fatigue and brake thermal degradation, worn/changed tire generations, calibration/configuration changes, missing or contradictory telemetry, and supplier/tool outages.

Tune numerical targets after baseline measurements are frozen. Report failed cases, uncertainty and missing data; never convert unmeasured values to zero.

## Evidence and safety boundaries

- Synthetic schema/optimizer pass != validated dynamics.
- Simulation pass != component durability or physical vehicle qualification.
- One prototype test != fleet reliability or manufacturing capability.
- Local assembly != local productive closure.
- Procedure authored != repair performed and independently checked.
- A benchmark result != roadworthiness, type approval or permission to operate.

Applicable references include ISO 4210-2/-6 for in-scope bicycle types, ISO 8710 for motorcycle brake test methods, ISO 26262-12 for motorcycle E/E functional-safety development (a new DIS is under enquiry as of 2026-10-18), UL 2849 for e-bike electrical systems where applicable, and ISO 14040 for lifecycle-assessment framework. Applicability and current local rules must be rechecked for the exact vehicle class and target market.

## Acceptance criteria

- Publish an owner map and non-duplication audit.
- Freeze at least one bicycle baseline protocol and explicit scenario manifest.
- Define scenario/result schemas with synthetic, simulated, workshop-measured, field-observed and regulatory evidence classes kept distinct.
- Include positive controls and seeded negative controls for configuration, unit, evidence, safety gate and economic-accounting errors.
- Define a staged qualification ladder from static checks through simulation, component/bench work, controlled track testing and independent legal/physical approval.
- Document benchmark commands/replay procedure or, if implementation is a later slice, explicitly label the current artefact documentation-only.
- State exact limitations and do not claim unexecuted build/test/CI results.

## Current scope ceiling

Planning and benchmark contracts only. No vehicle design is declared safe, optimized, affordable, manufacturable, roadworthy or certified by this issue.
